title: POC Weekly Sync - Dedicated Sizing & Autoscaling
summary: Weekly POC check-in to review recent pilot results, discuss Dedicated sizing, autoscaling policies and burst capacity. Customer shared updated traffic profile and stress test results. Agreed to run a 4-hour burst test on Dedicated pool and to share precise throughput numbers. Next steps: Redwood to propose autoscaling config and cost estimate; Maple to provide 7-day traffic histogram and acceptable latency SLOs.
next_steps: Redwood to send proposed Dedicated sizing + estimated monthly cost by 2025-06-05
Maple to share 7-day traffic histogram and 95th percentile latency target by 2025-06-04
Schedule 4-hour burst test next week, target 2x current peak, owner: Maple/Redwood ops
Priya to provide benchmark config (model variant, quantization) and how to run local validations
action_items: Alex Chen - draft Dedicated sizing options and cost breakdown - due 2025-06-05
Jordan Lee - export 7-day traffic histogram and current autoscaling triggers - due 2025-06-04
Priya Singh - attach benchmark runbook and recommended kernel settings in a Google doc - due 2025-06-03
Diego Ramos - share security questionnaire answers and SOC2 summary - due 2025-06-06
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-02 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Diego (CSM), Jordan (Maple SRE), Maria (Product), Ethan (Platform), Lila (Procurement)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick agenda — go over the pilot metrics you sent, talk about Dedicated sizing and autoscaling, and plan the burst test. Sound good?
[00:12] Jordan Lee: Yep, good. thanks, Alex. We had a brief sync this morning internally so hopefully we can be decisive.
[00:18] Maria Gomez: yeah, we want to understand cost implications and whether Dedicated will meet our SLA for 99th p95, p99 latency.
[00:26] Priya Singh: great, quick callout — we looked at the logs you shared, thanks — and we ran a few sample runs against the same model variant you used, the rdm-13b-q4 (note: transcription may say rdm-13b, model name sometimes garbled). The KV cache hit rate you're getting is around 22% in your sample, which is below what we'd expect for conversational workloads with stable prefixes.
[00:46] Ethan Park: oh, the cache number surprised us, we thought it was higher. That's from our side because of session IDs being new each time, client side isn't reusing prefixes reliably.
[00:57] Priya Singh: that will affect token cost and latency. If you can tweak the client to reuse conversation IDs we often see the hit rate jump to 45-60% for similar apps.
[01:08] Jordan Lee: noted, we're going to check that. From the stress test we did last night, the baseline peak qps was ~380 requests/sec with average payload ~220 tokens. Tail latencies at p95 were 320ms and p99 fairly spiky to 740ms.
[01:28] Alex Chen: thanks — do you have distribution by hour? 380 sounds like a current peak, do you expect burst multipliers?
[01:35] Jordan Lee: yes, we see occasional marketing driven spikes, historically up to 2.2x baseline during campaigns. So planning for burst capacity is a requirement.
[01:45] Priya Singh: ok, good to know. For Dedicated sizing, we typically propose a primary pool sized for steady state plus a burst pool or autoscaling headroom. The knobs we recommend: min replicas, desired replicas, max replicas, scale-up cooldown and scale-down cooldown, and a surge capacity buffer for short bursts.
[02:03] Maria Gomez: what are typical cooldowns? We had autoscale thrash in another product so worried about oscillation.
[02:09] Priya Singh: we usually recommend a 60-120s scale-up cooldown and a longer scale-down of 5-10 minutes to avoid thrash. For very spiky traffic you can use predictive autoscaling or a fast scale-up with limited burst capacity (e.g., allow 30% burst for 5 minutes).
[02:25] Ethan Park: can you quantify how many GPUs per 100 qps for our model? Our infra folks need concrete numbers.
[02:31] Priya Singh: rough ballpark for rdm-13b-q4 on A100-ish class is ~1 GPU per 110-140 qps when using batching and an optimized runtime; with quantization and lower sequence lengths your throughput improves. But that's sensitive to request token distribution.
[02:49] Jordan Lee: sequence length variance is high — some requests are 800 tokens. Those will kill throughput.
[02:55] Priya Singh: exactly; large sequences reduce qps significantly. For those, we recommend segregating long-context requests to their own route or model variant to avoid head-of-line blocking. Also consider progressive batching sizes and dynamic batching thresholds.
[03:12] Alex Chen: Diego, did you have notes on cost options we can share?
[03:16] Diego Ramos: yes, high level: Dedicated is priced by reserved GPU capacity. We'll give two proposals: conservative (steady-state + modest burst buffer) and aggressive (more reserved to flatten p99). We can show monthly estimates and per-token marginal cost differences.
[03:30] Lila Huang: procurement is particularly interested in minimum commitment and whether burst billing is separate.
[03:36] Alex Chen: good question. For Dedicated reserved capacity the commit covers baseline; burst usage can be billed as overage at a known rate or served from a shared hosted fallback if you want cost caping, we can show both models.
[03:50] Maria Gomez: is hosted fallback viable for us given data residency? some of our traffic must stay in-region.
[03:57] Priya Singh: we can pin regionally — Redwood Dedicated pools can be region specific. Hosted fallback would need to match your residency requirements. If not, we can instead configure an internal overprovisioned burst pool.
[04:12] Jordan Lee: on SLA, our target is p95 < 300ms and p99 < 700ms. We'd like conservative sizing to guarantee those numbers for 95% of traffic.
[04:22] Priya Singh: noted. Given your current p95 at 320ms and p99 spiky, I'd recommend sizing for peak qps times 1.3 headroom and configure a short burst buffer at 2.5x for up to 10 minutes for campaign spikes, with traffic routing to degrade to a smaller model variant if needed for cost control.
[04:46] Ethan Park: degradation path — how does that work? automatic fallback to smaller model?
[04:50] Priya Singh: yes, route policy can fallback to a quantized 7b variant or to a lower-res model with different latency profile. It's policy driven — you can prioritize latency over quality in defined routes.
[05:00] Alex Chen: quick interjection — we should also run a controlled 4-hour burst test at 2x and 3x to validate autoscale timings and cold-starts. Can we agree to that?
[05:10] Jordan Lee: yes, we can run it next Wednesday. We'll need Redwood to provide test harness and exact request patterns.
[05:17] Priya Singh: we'll package a harness and the sample scripts, plus a runbook outlining metrics to collect (CPU, GPU util, QPS, batching ratios, KV cache hit rate, latency percentiles).
[05:29] Maria Gomez: also please include guidance on tuning batching vs latency, because we can't accept big p99 regressions.
[05:35] Priya Singh: we'll include recommended batch sizes and how to adjust the continuous batching window. If your app requires strict p99, we may lower batch sizes and accept higher cost.
[05:45] Jordan Lee: what about KV cache — you said improving prefix reuse could reduce tokens by ~30-40%?
[05:51] Priya Singh: yes, in some cases. We will share a short doc on best practices for session affinity and prefix reuse.
[05:59] Alex Chen: Diego, is Redwood able to provide an estimated monthly cost for the two sizing options?
[06:03] Diego Ramos: yes, we'll run the numbers. We'll include a sensitivity table for different cache hit rates and different burst frequencies.
[06:12] Ethan Park: security question, quick — will Dedicated include audit logs and KMS integration?
[06:18] Priya Singh: yes, Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs with retention options. We'll attach the SOC2 summary you requested.
[06:27] Lila Huang: and procurement needs contract lead time — how long to onboard Dedicated once we sign?
[06:33] Alex Chen: onboarding time is typically 3-6 weeks depending on networking and KMS setup. We'll put the steps in the proposal.
[06:41] Maria Gomez: ok, any blockers from our side? Jordan?
[06:44] Jordan Lee: we need to clean up session IDs and run the histogram export. Also want to confirm the test window next Wednesday.
[06:52] Alex Chen: great — recap and owners, then we can close.
[06:55] Priya Singh: recap: Redwood to provide Dedicated sizing options, cost, burst-test harness and runbook; Maple to provide traffic histogram and run the 4-hour burst test; schedule follow-up after test to review results.
[07:07] Maria Gomez: sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:10] Alex Chen: thanks all. We'll follow up in email with the attachments and the proposed call for the test.

End transcript. Note: transcription contains occasional name/model garbling and timing approximations.
